title: Same-round resume for a limit-paused job via --continue; loop holds the slot
action: Per D3: execute_continue branches on job.json's paused_limit stamp — stamped AND recorded pane alive: deliver a same-round resume nudge ('your session was paused by a usage limit; continue the task and write the round-N result file at <path>') through the standard state-receipt delivery, clear the stamp (rewrite job.json without it), and re-enter wait_for_round for the SAME round; stamped but pane gone: typed refusal naming the pane loss. Unstamped jobs keep the existing next-round contract byte-identical. Per D4: wherever the control loop counts occupancy/unresolved workers, a paused_limit-stamped job's pane counts as occupied and its work is never re-dispatched while stamped — if the loop's occupancy already derives from unresolved ledger rows crossed with live panes, verify that a paused job stays unresolved and add a test pinning it; otherwise add the minimal check. Tests: stamped+alive resumes same round and clears stamp; stamped+gone refuses typed; unstamped continue unchanged.

truths: --continue on a stamped job with a live pane re-nudges the same round and clears the stamp
Next-round continue contract unchanged for unstamped jobs
A stamped job occupies its slot; its work is not re-dispatched
